research_question: When a new liquid crypto session opens on one side of the preceding session midpoint, does a causally confirmed 15-minute opening-range break and first retest deliver price to the corresponding preceding-session extreme often enough to support cost-positive day trading?

ideas_reused: opening range breakout after a fixed 15-minute balance
prior-session high or low as the causal liquidity objective
breakout close plus first retest instead of blind wick entry
external_mechanism.adaptation: Asia, London and New York liquidity handoffs are tested on BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT, SOLUSDT and XRPUSDT with cross-market breadth, actual structural stop/target geometry and a single global position.

data.source: Binance Vision USD-M monthly and daily one-minute klines
data.bar_visibility: one-minute bar is visible only at its close

fixed_rules.timeout_exit: last completed one-minute close before the fixed session evaluation horizon

scenario.context: new session opens above or below the preceding session midpoint
scenario.interaction: first 15-minute opening balance forms without consuming the objective
scenario.state: opening-range body, taker pressure and at least three of four peer paths align with the midpoint-selected direction
scenario.transition: first completed five-minute bar closes outside the opening range with aligned taker pressure
scenario.entry: first subsequent one-minute retest touches the broken opening-range edge and closes back outside
scenario.management: fixed target/stop or session timeout; no re-arm
scenario.no_trade: target consumed, mixed peer state, no breakout, no first retest or cost-adjusted structural R below 1.25

evaluation.same_session_arbitration: highest cost-adjusted structural R, then stronger breakout pressure, then symbol
evaluation.overlap_policy: no selected candidate while the current fixed stop/target/timeout trade is active

advance_gate.final_integrated_system_frequency_requir: at least one independent completed trade per evaluation calendar day after global arbitration

decision_contract.advance: Only the fixed integrated session family passing every declared split advances to NautilusTrader bracket-order validation.
decision_contract.reject: Do not optimize session times, opening-range length, breadth, stop, target or R thresholds after seeing the declared results.
